categories.main_business_segments: Cleveland-Cliffs operates primarily through its Steelmaking segment, which encompasses the production of flat-rolled carbon, stainless, electrical, and plate steel, as well as downstream operations in stamping, tooling, and tubing. Other businesses include Tubular Components and Tooling and Stamping, which provide carbon and stainless steel tubing, advanced-engineered solutions, and complex assemblies. The company also operates scrap processing facilities and maintains significant mining operations for iron ore and metallurgical coal.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Cliffs utilizes a vertically integrated production model, beginning with iron ore mining and pelletizing, direct reduction of iron (HBI), and ferrous scrap processing, followed by primary steelmaking using both blast furnaces (BOFs) and electric arc furnaces (EAFs). The company employs advanced steelmaking technologies, including the production of advanced high-strength steels (AHSS), grain-oriented and non-oriented electrical steels, and innovative downstream processes such as hot and cold stamping, tubular manufacturing, and tool and die making. The Toledo direct reduction plant is a key asset for producing low-carbon HBI, supporting decarbonization and flexibility in raw material sourcing.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Cliffs is the largest supplier of steel to the North American automotive industry, serving OEMs and their suppliers with high-quality, technologically advanced steel products. Other key markets include infrastructure and manufacturing (e.g., construction, HVAC, appliances, energy, and military), steel distributors and converters, and other steel producers who purchase raw materials and semi-finished goods. The company’s customer base is diversified across these sectors, with automotive accounting for a significant portion of revenues.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates primarily in the United States and Canada, with major steelmaking, mining, and scrap processing facilities concentrated in the Midwest and Great Lakes regions. Its iron ore mines are located in Michigan and Minnesota, while steelmaking and finishing plants are spread across Ohio, Indiana, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Illinois, West Virginia, and North Carolina. The vast majority of sales are to North American customers, with limited international exposure.
categories.supply_chain_position: Cleveland-Cliffs is a vertically integrated steel producer, operating from upstream (iron ore mining and pelletizing, scrap processing, and HBI production) through midstream (primary steelmaking) to downstream (finishing, stamping, tooling, and tubing). This integration allows the company to control raw material inputs, production processes, and finished product delivery, reducing reliance on external suppliers and enhancing cost predictability.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategically, Cliffs focuses on maximizing its commercial strengths in high-value markets (especially automotive), optimizing its fully integrated footprint, expanding its presence in ferrous scrap recycling, and advancing participation in the green economy through decarbonization and support for electric vehicles and renewable energy. R&D initiatives emphasize the development of advanced high-strength steels, electrical steels for EVs and grid modernization, and innovative downstream applications. The company is committed to reducing GHG emissions by 25% from 2017 levels by 2030 and invests in energy efficiency, carbon capture, and sustainable production technologies.
categories.revenue_model: Cliffs generates revenue primarily through the sale of steel products (flat-rolled, coated, stainless, electrical, and plate steels), iron ore pellets, HBI, scrap, and downstream products such as tubing and stamped components. Approximately 45% of steel volumes are sold under annual fixed-price contracts, particularly to automotive customers, while the remainder is sold on the spot market or under index-linked contracts. The company also derives revenue from long-term supply agreements for raw materials and semi-finished goods.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include domestic and foreign steel producers such as U.S. Steel, Nucor, and ArcelorMittal, as well as mini-mills and alternative material suppliers (e.g., aluminum producers). Cliffs is the largest flat-rolled steel producer and the largest supplier of automotive-grade steel in North America, with unique capabilities in electrical steels and a comprehensive product portfolio. Its vertically integrated model and control over raw materials provide a competitive advantage in cost, quality, and supply chain resilience.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2021, Cleveland-Cliffs reported record revenues of $20.4 billion, net income of $3.0 billion, and Adjusted EBITDA of $5.3 billion, reflecting transformational growth following the acquisitions of AK Steel and ArcelorMittal USA. The company produced 18 million net tons of raw steel and employed approximately 26,000 people. Its growth trajectory has been marked by significant expansion in scale, product offerings, and vertical integration, with strong free cash flow supporting debt reduction and shareholder returns.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Cliffs’ value proposition centers on its ability to deliver high-quality, technologically advanced steel products—especially for demanding automotive and electrical applications—supported by a fully integrated, environmentally responsible supply chain. The company differentiates itself through its leadership in automotive-grade and electrical steels, comprehensive product range, proximity to customers, and commitment to sustainability and decarbonization. Its vertical integration ensures cost stability, supply security, and responsiveness to customer needs.
